title: H-plane 90° radius bend of WR-90 (inner radius 28.6 mm, arms 20 mm): S21 against the continuously curved guide's dominant mode
source: The curved guide's modes (Cochran & Pecina, Radio Science 1(6), 1966; Lewin, Chang & Kuester 1977): ν₀ by Chebyshev collocation of ρ²u″ + ρu′ + (k²ρ² − ν²)u = 0, u = 0 on both walls (Trefethen 2000), settled to 1e-12; the junctions to the straight arms by Rice's matrix theory (BSTJ 27(2), 1948): the curved modes in the straight ones, matched mode by mode with 80 modes (40 to 80 modes moves S by under 1e-6); emcraft-theory's `curved::bend`, moved to the arms' ends by e^{−2jβ·20 mm}

quantities.reason: second-order elements of 3 mm and an arc of 18 chords on the radius whose chords' mean distance from the centre is the arc's (an inscribed polygon is 0.3° fast): measured within 0.12°. The leading term −ν₀π/2 − 2βl alone is within 0.18° of the reference, the junctions' O(|S11|) correction
lossless: |S21|² = 1 − |S11|², |S11| < 0.006, so |S21| is 1 to 2e-5 and the FEM conserves power to rounding

Rice's junction reflection, computed by `curved::junction`, is at most 0.0041 over the band ((a/R)² = 0.33 times a small factor); two junctions add at most 2 × 0.0041 = 0.0082, with 0.002 for the chords' corners and the mesh (the measured |S11| follows the mode matching's 0.0007 to 0.0051 within 7e-4)
